repo_notes.content: Vault Cortex is a remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes an Obsidian vault over HTTPS — vault CRUD, hybrid search, task management, structured memory, link-graph queries, and non-markdown file reading (images, PDFs, canvases, data files), plus user-initiated prompts. It runs headless in Docker, working directly with .md files on disk using its own Obsidian-parity parsers and search index. README.md is the authoritative feature description and ARCHITECTURE.md the authoritative design document — derive capability details, defaults, and security specifics from those and the code rather than restating them. The repo also ships a CLI (cli/, published as the vault-cortex npm package) that scaffolds a deployment: npx vault-cortex@latest init.

The codebase is organized into four internal layers under src/vault-mcp/: (1) obsidian-markdown/ — pure Obsidian/Markdown parsers with no I/O (links, lines/fences, frontmatter, callouts, headings, tasks, memory entries, canvas, plaintext). (2) vault-operations/ — filesystem I/O for vault content (vault-filesystem, vault-patcher, note-mover, memory-store, daily-notes, task-mutations, task-format-config, asset-operations). (3) search/ — the SQLite FTS5 + sqlite-vec index, embedding pipeline, and chokidar file watcher. (4) mcp-core/ — the MCP protocol surface: streamable-http transport, tool group modules under mcp-core/tools/, and prompt group modules under mcp-core/prompts/. Authentication lives in src/vault-mcp/oauth/ (OAuth 2.1) and src/functions/authorizer.ts (AWS Lambda, path-aware). Infrastructure-as-code (sst.config.ts) is specific to the AWS reference deployment and should not be documented as the primary deployment path.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What Vault Cortex is and does, drawn from the current README.md: an MCP server giving AI agents hybrid search, task management, structured memory, non-markdown file reading, and read/write access to an Obsidian vault. The ways to run it are covered on the Deployment page. Summarize the README's value proposition as it stands at index time rather than a fixed capability list.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Quickstart paths from README.md and deploy/: local Docker, one-click on Render or Railway, self-hosted on a VPS with Obsidian Sync, and the AWS reference deployment. Also covers MCP client configuration. The npx vault-cortex@latest init CLI is the fastest path for the local and VPS modes.

pages.title: CLI
pages.purpose: The vault-cortex npm package under cli/ — the deployment-management commands defined in cli/src/program.ts, their interactive and non-interactive flows, and the module structure under cli/src/. Enumerate the commands from program.ts at index time rather than restating them.

pages.title: Configuration Reference
pages.purpose: All environment variables as defined in config.ts and the .env.example files, the ServerConfig type, and how configuration differs across the deployment modes. Enumerate the variables from the source at index time.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Parent page providing an overview of the four-layer internal architecture (obsidian-markdown, vault-operations, search, mcp-core), the data flow from MCP client request through transport to data layer and back, and the component diagram showing how Obsidian Sync, the vault filesystem, SQLite, and the MCP server interact. ARCHITECTURE.md is the authoritative source.

pages.title: Server and Transport
pages.purpose: How the Express server bootstraps (server.ts), the MCP streamable-http transport lifecycle (mcp-core/mcp-router.ts), session management, and the logger chain that flows context (sessionId, clientIp, requestId, tool) through child loggers.

pages.title: Authentication and Security
pages.purpose: The two-layer auth model: the AWS Lambda authorizer (src/functions/authorizer.ts, path-aware) and the OAuth 2.1 provider (src/vault-mcp/oauth/), plus the shared utilities in src/auth.ts and src/jwt.ts. Also covers the runtime-hardening posture — derive the specifics from ARCHITECTURE.md's Data integrity section and SECURITY.md.

pages.title: Obsidian Markdown Parsing
pages.purpose: The pure parser layer in obsidian-markdown/ — no filesystem I/O: links.ts, lines.ts, frontmatter.ts, callouts.ts, headings.ts, tasks.ts, memory-entries.ts, canvas.ts, plaintext.ts, moment-format.ts. This layer encodes the Obsidian-parity behavior (every link form and 'New link format' mode Obsidian recognizes; both Tasks-plugin formats) that distinguishes Vault Cortex from simpler file-based integrations.

pages.title: Vault Operations
pages.purpose: The filesystem I/O layer in vault-operations/: vault-filesystem.ts (base primitives including atomic writes and path safety), vault-patcher.ts, note-mover.ts, memory-store.ts, daily-notes.ts, task-mutations.ts, task-format-config.ts, and asset-operations.ts (the use-case behind vault_read_file and vault_list_files). Derive the safety mechanisms (locking modes, TOCTOU guards, protected paths) from ARCHITECTURE.md's Data integrity section.

pages.title: Search and Indexing
pages.purpose: The SQLite FTS5 + sqlite-vec search system in search/. Modules: search-index.ts (factory, schema, write operations); search-queries.ts (query methods and the SearchQueryContext shape); hybrid-search.ts (the hybrid search pipeline); search-helpers.ts (pure transforms); fts-query.ts (FTS5 sanitization); rrf.ts (RRF fusion); reranker.ts (cross-encoder reranking and score blending); embedder.ts and chunker.ts (embedding pipeline); file-watcher.ts (chokidar). Covers hybrid search and its FTS-only fallback, the memory-entry index, the non_md_files table, and the tasks table. Derive ranking details, models, and defaults from ARCHITECTURE.md's Hybrid Search section.

pages.title: Memory Layer
pages.purpose: The About Me/ memory system: memory-store.ts, the memory-entry grammar in obsidian-markdown/memory-entries.ts, the entry-granular recall index, and the templates/memory/ bootstrap templates. The layer is opt-out via MEMORY_ENABLED.

pages.title: Task Management
pages.purpose: The Tasks-plugin domain across layers: the task-line grammar in obsidian-markdown/tasks.ts (emoji and Dataview inline-field formats, read and write), task-mutations.ts mutations, task-format-config.ts (the user's Tasks-plugin format configuration), the tasks table in the search index, and the task tools under mcp-core/tools/. Derive status, priority, and date-signifier specifics from the source at index time.

pages.title: Non-Markdown Files
pages.purpose: How non-markdown vault files (images, PDFs, canvases, text and data files) are read, browsed, and searched. Modules: asset-operations.ts (the use-case layer behind the file tools); canvas.ts (JSON Canvas to readable markdown); fit-image-to-byte-budget.ts (image byte-budget fitting); obsidian-markdown/pdf-engine.ts (the pdfjs bootstrap); obsidian-markdown/pdf.ts (PDF text extraction); the file_content and file_content_fts tables in the search index. Derive supported formats and size limits from the source at index time.

pages.title: MCP Interface
pages.purpose: Parent page for the MCP protocol surface — tools (model-driven) and prompts (user-initiated), both assembling live vault content. Structure: tool group modules under mcp-core/tools/, declared in tool-registry.ts and composed by tool-definitions.ts; prompt group modules under mcp-core/prompts/ composed by prompt-definitions.ts.

pages.title: Tool Reference
pages.purpose: The MCP tools by domain group module under mcp-core/tools/: vault-crud-tools.ts, search-tools.ts, task-tools.ts, memory-tools.ts (registered when MEMORY_ENABLED is true), daily-note-tools.ts, and asset-tools.ts (vault_read_file and vault_list_files, registered when FILE_TOOLS_ENABLED is true). Derive each tool's inputs and behavior from its registration in the source — descriptions follow an Example / When to use / Returns / Errors structure.

pages.title: Prompt Reference
pages.purpose: The MCP prompts under mcp-core/prompts/: vault-orientation, memory-review, and daily-review, with prompt-definitions.ts as the orchestrator. Each assembles live vault data at invocation time and degrades to a valid fallback message rather than throwing.

pages.title: Deployment
pages.purpose: Parent page for the four ways to run the server: local Docker, one-click on Render or Railway, self-hosted on a VPS with Obsidian Sync, and the AWS reference deployment. Every mode runs an image from the single two-target Dockerfile. The :latest target is the MCP server alone, for local. The :remote target adds Obsidian Sync under s6-overlay supervision, for everything else. Quickstarts live in deploy/; the CLI scaffolds the local and VPS ones.

pages.title: Local Docker Deployment
pages.purpose: The deploy/local/ quickstart: a single container with the vault folder bind-mounted from the host, no cloud services. Includes Windows bind-mount support (WINDOWS_MODE).

pages.title: Remote Deployment with Obsidian Sync
pages.purpose: The deploy/remote/ quickstart for a VPS: the :remote image with named Docker volumes, where s6-overlay supervises the Obsidian Sync process and the MCP server (service definitions and init chain in rootfs/). Requires an Obsidian Sync subscription and an HTTPS front. This is the self-hosted route to mobile and remote access; the one-click route is on the Hosted Platform Templates page.

pages.title: AWS Reference Deployment
pages.purpose: The reference deployment provisioned by sst.config.ts and documented in DEPLOY.md: a Lightsail instance running the :remote image, API Gateway for TLS, and a path-aware Lambda authorizer. It is one worked option, not a requirement; Vault Cortex runs anywhere Docker does.

pages.title: Hosted Platform Templates
pages.purpose: The one-click deployments of the :remote image on Render and Railway. Both run the image in single-volume mode: STORAGE_ROOT names the one mount and print-derived-env in rootfs/ derives PUBLIC_URL from the platform. Render deploys from render.yaml at the repo root, documented in deploy/render/. Railway deploys from a template built in its composer, whose definition is recorded in CONTRIBUTING.md. cli/src/__tests__/templates.test.ts pins render.yaml and the Railway definition table.

pages.title: Container Image and Process Supervision
pages.purpose: The two-target Dockerfile that builds both images from one file. The local target is tini plus the MCP server. The remote target is s6-overlay supervising the obsidian-sync and MCP server processes. Also covers the rootfs/ filesystem overlay (s6 service definitions and init chain), the lockfile-pinned obsidian-headless/ package, and runtime user handling (PUID/PGID). Derive base-image and version specifics from the Dockerfile at index time.

pages.title: Development Guide
pages.purpose: Contributing to Vault Cortex: local development setup (npm run dev, docker-compose.local.yml), the vitest test suite, the structured JSON logging system (logger.ts and the child-logger context chain), and contribution conventions. References CONTRIBUTING.md.

pages.title: Release and CI Pipeline
pages.purpose: The GitHub Actions workflows under .github/workflows/: CI checks, server and CLI release automation, deployment workflows, security scanning, and registry publishing. Also the dev/ops helper scripts under scripts/. Enumerate the workflows and their triggers from the workflow files at index time; release conventions live in CONTRIBUTING.md.
